description:
REVIEWED 2026-10-25 (TodoReview) against origin/develop 9a184b619 and fork main ea44bcc9 (30.24.0.13). PROBLEM
In the published SQLite ClickBench SF1 bundle `clickbench_sf1_sqlite_sql_20260824_101152_6eb94fe6` most queries return row counts that differ from every other engine. A rerun alone will not fix it (the SQL changed only for Q19 and Q43 since v0.4.1). Cause unknown; found by the published-results audit (history://AffectedResults), noted in results-data/CORPUS_NOTES.md by #3398.

VERIFIED FACTS (2026-10-25)
- Counted from the bundle files: SQLite matches DuckDB row counts on only 17 of the 40 queries that succeeded; 26 of 43 queries differ from the consensus of the other engines: Q19, Q29, Q43 FAILED (errors: `near "FROM": syntax error`, `no such function: REGEXP_REPLACE`, `no such function: DATE_TRUNC`; 9 failed executions of 129 in `summary.queries`) and 23 returned wrong counts (Q8 1 vs 20, Q9 1 vs 10, Q10 1 vs 10, Q11-Q15 0 vs 9/10, Q16-Q18 1 vs 10, Q22, Q24-Q27, Q31, Q32, Q38 0 vs 10, Q34/Q35 1 vs 8, Q36 1 vs 10, Q37 0 vs 8). The 'about 25 of 43' figure in the item and CORPUS_NOTES.md is approximately right; Q29 (no REGEXP_REPLACE on SQLite) is not mentioned in CORPUS_NOTES, which says only Q19 and Q43 'failed before and now run'.
- The other nine engines agree with DuckDB on all 43 queries (Databricks differs on two: see databricks-clickbench-q29-q43-result-mismatch).
- Local probe on origin/develop 9a184b619, SF0.01 (10,000 rows), SQLiteAdapter vs DuckDBAdapter on the same generated `hits.tbl`: the SQLite load keeps the two-character literal `""` where the shard has quoted empty strings and DuckDB reads an empty string. `min(MobilePhoneModel)` = '""' vs ''; `count(*) WHERE MobilePhoneModel <> ''` = 10000 vs 1502; `SearchPhrase <> ''` 10000 vs 2579; Q11 and Q12 return 10 vs 9 rows. This is a reproducible loader defect on current develop and a prime candidate, but it does NOT explain the published SF1 bundle by itself: the published counts are LOWER (Q11-Q15 zero rows), the opposite direction, and Q8 (`AdvEngineID <> 0`) matches at SF0.01 (21 groups both) but was 1 vs 20 at SF1. So the bundle was produced with different data or loader code, or a second defect exists at 1M rows. Treat both as open until an SF1 comparison on current develop is done.
- The published bundle recorded 1,000,000 rows loaded, validation `partial`.

DECISION GATES (stop and ask the owner)
G1 Fix layer once the cause is classified. Options: (a) SQLite loader/adapter normalises quoted empty fields for ClickBench (recommended if the `""` cause is confirmed at SF1); (b) change the ClickBench generator to write true empty fields (changes generated data for every platform and its published-dataset provenance; benchmark-data definition change, needs approval); (c) a registered SQLite skip with reason for queries SQLite cannot run (Q29 REGEXP_REPLACE, Q43 DATE_TRUNC if still failing) - acceptable only per query with a reason, never for wrong-count queries.
G2 Flagging the published bundle. The existing `defective-superseded-sql-translation` id describes SQL, not a load defect. Options: reuse it (misleading), add a new closed-vocabulary id such as `defective-sqlite-clickbench-results` (changes the results policy vocabulary; owner approval), or a CORPUS_NOTES-only note (current state). Recommended: new id if the bundle's recorded rows are wrong (they are for 23 queries), applied to the sidecar only.
G3 Publishing a rerun bundle into the corpus is a publication step (owner approval; see flagged-local-bundles-compliance-class-gate-20261025 for the validator gate).

GUARDRAILS
- Never edit the published bundle JSON; sidecar `known_defects` + CORPUS_NOTES only.
- Never change a query or an expected answer so SQLite 'matches'; never skip a wrong-count query to hide it.
- SQLite SF1 loads are heavy: generate data under a temp or BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR outside the repo, one heavy run at a time, no raw broad pytest runs.
- No cloud spend. Real engines only: compare against DuckDB on the same generated data, not against recorded bundle numbers alone.

STANDING GUARDRAILS: work only in a `make worktree-create` worktree after `make agent-write-preflight` (primary clone /Users/joe/Developer/BenchBox is read-only); run tests only through make targets (`make test-fast`, `make pr-preflight`, `make sql-execution-gate`, `make tpcds-obt-equivalence`) or targeted `uv run -- python -m pytest <paths> -n 4`; never BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR, `make test-unlock` or raw broad runs; one heavy run at a time; no live-cloud spend and no production publish without explicit owner approval; published result bundles are never edited (only manifest-sidecar `known_defects` and results-data/CORPUS_NOTES.md per results-data/DEFECTIVE_DATAGEN_AUDIT.md); no SKIP / --no-verify / `git add -A`; no explanatory comments or docstrings in code (`make comment-policy-check`); uv only; identity Joe Harris, no Co-Authored-By; PR flow `make pr-preflight` once, `make pr-open`, CI + oracle review, `make pr-arm`. Stop and ask the owner on unexpected result changes, relaxed guards, oracle stand-ins or real design choices.
